classification.difficultyReason: Recall the horizontal-shift sign rule, supported by labelled example graphs and the supplied initial letters of right and left.

content.prompt: Consider the parabolas of the form $(x\pm b)^2$:

spec.description: Common square grid and axes comparing the red reference parabola with its blue translation three units left. Origin O omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Reference y=x^2; comparison y=(x+3)^2; vertices (0,0) and (-3,0). Grid step 2 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and their equations are permanent student-visible givens.

spec.description: Common square grid and axes comparing the red reference parabola with its blue translation one unit right. Origin O omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Reference y=x^2; comparison y=(x-1)^2; vertices (0,0) and (1,0). Grid step 2 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and their equations are permanent student-visible givens.

spec.description: Common square grid and axes comparing the red reference parabola with its blue translation two units right. Origin O omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Reference y=x^2; comparison y=(x-2)^2; vertices (0,0) and (2,0). Grid step 2 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and their equations are permanent student-visible givens.

spec.description: Common square grid and axes comparing the red reference parabola with its blue translation four units left. Origin O omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Reference y=x^2; comparison y=(x+4)^2; vertices (0,0) and (-4,0). Grid step 2 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and their equations are permanent student-visible givens.

inlines.text: , the parabola translates to the r

answer.worked: The turning point moves from $(0,0)$ to $(b,0)$. Since $b>0$, the parabola translates right by $b$ units.

inlines.text: , the parabola translates to the l

answer.worked: The turning point moves from $(0,0)$ to $(-b,0)$. Since $b>0$, the parabola translates left by $b$ units.
